question: Which of the following is a primary way the community environment influences health?

options.A: Replacing the need for individual personal hygiene
options.B: Providing access to safe water, markets, and local clinics
options.C: Ensuring every citizen has a high-paying professional job
options.D: Eliminating all infectious diseases from the environment

explanation: Basic community infrastructure like clean water and nearby health clinics directly dictates physical well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is it important for nurses to review immunization registers regularly?

options.A: To calculate monthly staff salary and allowances
options.B: To identify children who have missed scheduled doses and need tracking
options.C: To find out which vaccine brand is most expensive
options.D: To report families to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Regular register checks help nurses spot missing children early so they can organize follow-up visits before outbreaks happen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h6)

question: A patient is prescribed a metered-dose inhaler without a spacer and complains that the medicine just hits their throat. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Instruct the patient to hold their breath for five minutes after inhaling
options.B: Call the doctor to change the prescription to a skin patch
options.C: Advise the patient to obtain and use a spacer device to improve drug delivery
options.D: Tell the patient to swallow the medicine instead of breathing it in

explanation: Spacers act as a holding chamber that slows down the spray, preventing medication from depositing in the mouth and throat instead of the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h4)

question: Who is most likely to require custodial care over a long period?

options.A: An athlete recovering from a simple sports-related ankle sprain
options.B: A patient with a sudden bacterial infection needing a short antibiotic course
options.C: A person admitted to the emergency ward with acute appendicitis
options.D: An individual with chronic physical disabilities or severe cognitive loss

explanation: People with chronic disabilities or long-term cognitive decline often lose the ability to care for themselves independently, making custodial support necessary. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when estimating injection commodity needs?

options.A: Performing regular physical inventory audits on the ward
options.B: Ignoring existing stock levels currently sitting in the storeroom
options.C: Collaborating closely with pharmacy and supply chain personnel
options.D: Reviewing past consumption reports from previous months

explanation: Always subtract what is already in stock from your calculated requirement so you do not accidentally over-order. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h6)

question: Which substances were historically harvested directly from animals for medical use?

options.A: Petroleum-based solvents
options.B: Pure mineral salts and water
options.C: Synthetic plastics and nylon
options.D: Hormones and insulin

explanation: Before lab technology advanced, we relied heavily on animal organs—like pig and cow pancreases—to get insulin for diabetic patients.

question: What is the most critical check a nurse must do before giving penicillin for the first time?

options.A: Measuring the patient head circumference
options.B: Checking for a history of drug allergies
options.C: Evaluating the patient visual acuity score
options.D: Assessing the patient daily fluid intake

explanation: Safety first! Always check for allergies. A patient with a severe penicillin allergy can crash quickly from anaphylaxis if you miss this step.

question: During a surgical hand scrub, which way should the rinse water always flow?

options.A: From elbows down toward the fingertips
options.B: Upward toward the shoulders and neck
options.C: Straight off the hands without dripping
options.D: From fingertips down toward the elbows

explanation: Water should flow from cleanest (fingertips) to less clean (elbows) so dirty water never runs back down over your hands.

question: If a hospital uses all its DRF cash to fix a broken generator, what happens first?

options.A: The hospital will immediately receive a large grant from the ministry
options.B: Patients will start buying cheaper drugs from the hospital store
options.C: The cost of electricity in the wards will drop significantly
options.D: The pharmacy will soon run out of money to restock essential drugs

explanation: That breaks the rule of ring-fencing! Without cash in the revolving account, new medicine orders can't be placed, leading straight to empty shelves.

question: Why do many people in local communities prefer getting injections from informal medicine shops?

options.A: Oral medications are completely unavailable in cities
options.B: Government policy requires informal shops to give shots
options.C: They believe injections work much faster than pills
options.D: Injections are always cheaper than tablets

explanation: It's a common belief that shooting medicine straight into the body heals you faster than swallowing a pill. As nurses, patient education on safe administration is key here!

question: What is a major risk of overfeeding a critically ill patient on a ventilator?

options.A: Extra carbon dioxide production making it harder to breathe off the ventilator
options.B: Total elimination of the need for IV fluids
options.C: Rapid healing of surgical wounds
options.D: A sudden drop in blood sugar levels

explanation: Giving too many calories—especially from carbs—makes the body produce extra carbon dioxide. This makes breathing much harder for a patient trying to come off a ventilator!

question: What happens to nutrients during metabolism after your body absorbs them?

options.A: They circulate in the blood without undergoing any changes
options.B: They are immediately eliminated as solid waste products
options.C: They are used for immediate energy or stored for later use
options.D: They are turned back into large, whole food particles

explanation: Once absorbed, metabolism kicks in: your cells either burn the nutrients right away for energy or stash them away as reserves for later.

question: In research, what does the term 'reliability' mean?

options.A: Whether the tool measures what it is supposed to measure
options.B: The speed at which the patient answers interview questions
options.C: Consistency of results when using a tool repeatedly
options.D: How expensive the laboratory equipment is to purchase

explanation: Spot on! If a tool is reliable, it gives you stable, dependable results every time you use it under the same conditions.

question: What is the main purpose of the blood-testis barrier created by Sertoli cells?

options.A: To filter out excess water from the seminal fluid
options.B: To prevent the immune system from attacking developing sperm cells
options.C: To stop bacteria from traveling upward from the urinary tract
options.D: To maintain high blood pressure inside the seminiferous tubules

explanation: Because developing sperm have unique proteins, the blood-testis barrier shields them from being attacked by white blood cells. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which hormone helps your body handle long-term stress?

options.A: Melatonin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Cortisol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: You nailed it! Cortisol is your body's main stress manager, helping you cope with physical and emotional pressure over time.

question: Why does waste material become hard and dry when it moves too slowly through the colon?

options.A: The liver stops producing mucus to lubricate the intestinal walls
options.B: The anal sphincter closes too tightly and squeezes out moisture
options.C: Bacteria in the lower bowel multiply rapidly and dry out the waste
options.D: Extra time allows the colon to absorb more water than normal

explanation: Makes sense, right? If stool stays too long in the colon, the body keeps drawing out water, leaving the waste dry and tough to pass.

question: What should a patient do right after coughing into a disposable tissue?

options.A: Place the tissue in their pocket for later use
options.B: Leave the tissue on the bedside table
options.C: Hand the tissue directly to the attending nurse
options.D: Throw the tissue in the trash and clean their hands

explanation: Correct! Tossing the tissue straight into the bin and cleaning up stops those sneaky germs from spreading to bed tables or other people.

question: Why is an oxygen tent not the best choice when a patient needs very high oxygen levels?

options.A: The plastic material is chemically unable to hold high pressure
options.B: Opening the canopy to care for the patient causes the oxygen level to drop
options.C: Adults consume too much oxygen for the tent motor to handle
options.D: High oxygen levels melt the seals of the canopy frame

explanation: Every time you unzip or open the tent to check on the child or feed them, the trapped oxygen escapes quickly into the room air.

question: When a patient has a blood disorder, why must you check multiple body systems instead of just one area?

options.A: Haematological disorders only affect the skin and the muscles
options.B: Blood circulates throughout the entire body and impacts every organ
options.C: Blood cell counts change completely every single hour
options.D: Hospital protocols require checking every organ for all patients

explanation: Remember, blood travels everywhere! Because it touches every part of the body, a blood problem can show up as symptoms in different organs.

question: What is the highest possible score on a standard muscle strength testing scale?

options.A: Ten
options.B: One hundred
options.C: Three
options.D: Five

explanation: Muscle power is graded from 0 to 5. A score of 5 means the patient has normal strength and can push hard against your full resistance.

question: A patient hears voices when no one is around. What do we call this?

options.A: Delusion
options.B: Flight of ideas
options.C: Hallucination
options.D: Concrete thinking

explanation: Great job! Hearing things that aren't actually there is an auditory hallucination. Keep up the good work!

question: What is the main goal of fracture reduction?

options.A: To permanently increase the overall length of the injured limb
options.B: To dissolve any blood clots that formed around the injury site
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for any pain medication
options.D: To restore the broken bone fragments back into proper anatomical alignment

explanation: Reduction simply means putting the broken bone ends back in their correct place so they can heal straight and strong.

question: When you face sudden stress, which two key hormones do your adrenal glands rush out?

options.A: Adrenaline and cortisol
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: Adrenaline gives you that instant rush of energy (fight or flight), while cortisol helps keep your energy up to handle the stressor.

question: A nurse is teaching a patient how to do Kegel exercises correctly. What is the key instruction?

options.A: Contract the pelvic floor muscles as if trying to stop the flow of urine
options.B: Squeeze the abdominal and thigh muscles tightly while holding your breath
options.C: Push down gently as if having a bowel movement
options.D: Flex the buttocks and hips until your pelvis rises off the bed

explanation: Spot on! Kegels are all about squeezing those pelvic floor muscles—just like you're pausing your urine stream mid-flow, without squeezing your tummy or thighs.

question: A patient presents with extreme fatigue, pale skin, and spoon-shaped fingernails. Which deficiency is most likely present?

options.A: Vitamin E
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Thiamine
options.D: Iron

explanation: These are classic signs of iron-deficiency anemia, where reduced hemoglobin levels impair oxygen delivery to tissues. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h6)

question: How do voluntary agencies usually work alongside government health services?

options.A: They completely take over ministry duties
options.B: They compete fiercely for patients
options.C: They complement and support public services
options.D: They regulate medical licensing in the country

explanation: Spot on! They don't try to replace government hospitals; instead, they team up to fill gaps and reach people who need help most.

question: Why do modern hospitals emphasize respectful maternity care?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any medical issues
options.B: It reduces the cost of building new maternity wards
options.C: It encourages women to choose facility delivery instead of staying home
options.D: It replaces the need for any medications during labor

explanation: Nobody wants to visit a harsh nurse! When women feel welcomed and valued in the clinic, they are happy to come back for safe deliveries.

question: What is the main function of the Bartholin glands?

options.A: Release hormones that trigger puberty
options.B: Protect the pubic bone from physical shock
options.C: Secrete lubricating mucus into the vestibule
options.D: Produce eggs during the monthly cycle

explanation: Bartholin glands sit beside the vaginal opening and produce mucus to keep the mucosal surface moist. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why is teaching a core part of your job as a nurse?

options.A: It helps patients manage illnesses and prevent complications
options.B: It replaces the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: It ensures the hospital receives higher financial grants
options.D: It is only required when students are completing clinical rotations

explanation: You spend the most time with patients! Teaching them how to care for themselves at home is one of the best ways to keep them safe and out of the hospital.

question: Which chart is best for showing how patient vital signs change over time?

options.A: Frequency table
options.B: Pie chart
options.C: Bar chart
options.D: Line graph

explanation: You got it! Whenever you want to track changes over a timeline—like hourly blood pressure readings—a line graph is your best friend.

question: What is the primary purpose of an Institutional Review Board (IRB) in research?

options.A: To provide financial grants and equipment to student researchers
options.B: To grade the academic performance of nursing postgraduate students
options.C: To market the finished research paper to private pharmaceutical companies
options.D: To protect the rights, safety, and well-being of human research subjects

explanation: An ethics committee or IRB reviews study proposals beforehand to make sure human participants will not be harmed or exploited. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why should you avoid twisting your body while carrying a heavy load?

options.A: It causes the rescue team to lose their sense of direction
options.B: It increases the air pressure inside the transport vehicle
options.C: It automatically makes the patient slide off the stretcher
options.D: It places excessive rotational stress on the lumbar spine disks

explanation: That's correct! Twisting while carrying something heavy is one of the fastest ways nurses hurt their lower backs. Protect your spine!

question: What type of feedback loop does the body mostly use to keep hormone levels balanced?

options.A: Negative feedback loops
options.B: Neutral feedback loops
options.C: External feedback loops
options.D: Positive feedback loops

explanation: Negative feedback is like a home thermostat. When hormone levels get too high, a signal tells the gland to slow down and stop making more until things are balanced again.

question: How does poor nutrition in a pregnant mother directly affect her unborn baby?

options.A: It prevents the development of neonatal jaundice entirely
options.B: It causes the baby to be born with complete immunity to infections
options.C: It accelerates the closure of the infant's fontanelles
options.D: It increases the risk of low birth weight and developmental stunting

explanation: A baby's growth depends totally on what the mother eats. Poor maternal nutrition often leads to low birth weight babies who have a harder time fighting off sickness.

question: What is the main rule for any food or drink included in a fluid diet?

options.A: It must contain high amounts of protein and fiber.
options.B: It must require extensive chewing before swallowing.
options.C: It must be liquid at room or body temperature.
options.D: It must be served exclusively at a warm temperature.

explanation: Think of a fluid diet as anything that turns or stays liquid as it warms up in the mouth or stomach. Simple and easy to remember!

question: How do anticholinergic drugs stop cells from being activated at the receptor site?

options.A: By blocking acetylcholine production in the liver
options.B: By competitively binding to the receptors
options.C: By destroying existing acetylcholine molecules
options.D: By speeding up cellular metabolism

explanation: Well done! These drugs sit on the receptor sites first so acetylcholine can't attach to trigger a response.

question: What is the main purpose of the systemic circulation?

options.A: Filter waste products in the kidneys
options.B: Remove carbon dioxide from the lungs
options.C: Warm up blood before it reaches the brain
options.D: Deliver oxygenated blood to body tissues

explanation: The systemic circuit is responsible for pumping oxygen and nutrients out to all body organs and tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h1)

question: A hospital committee is choosing between a brand-new, super expensive painkiller and an older, cheap one that works almost as well. What should they do?

options.A: Stock it only for patients who complain about older drugs
options.B: Buy large quantities to impress visiting health inspectors
options.C: Accept it immediately to stay modern and technologically advanced
options.D: Reject it because it fails the cost-effectiveness principle

explanation: You nailed it! As nurses and health planners, we always balance the health benefit against the cost to ensure wise spending.

question: A community health nurse opens a delivery kit and finds a soap bar, a plastic sheet, a cord tie, a razor blade, and a cloth. What is the primary role of the razor blade?

options.A: To open other plastic packaging
options.B: To rupture the amniotic sac
options.C: To clean the mother's skin
options.D: To cut the umbilical cord

explanation: The razor blade serves as the sterile instrument dedicated to cutting the umbilical cord cleanly. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h2)

question: Which type of transmission involves bugs like mosquitoes or ticks passing on an infection?

options.A: Airborne droplet spread
options.B: Direct physical contact
options.C: Common vehicle transmission
options.D: Vector-borne transmission

explanation: Vectors are living bugs and insects that carry pathogens from one place to another—think of mosquitoes and malaria!

question: What happens when hospital administrators treat MBO as just a bureaucratic checklist?

options.A: Patient satisfaction increases across all departments
options.B: The hospital saves money on administrative salaries
options.C: Staff quickly lose interest and trust in the process
options.D: Nurses become expert planners overnight

explanation: When MBO lacks genuine leadership commitment and becomes mere paperwork, staff view it as a burden rather than a useful tool. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h6)

question: What makes 'probability sampling' special compared to other methods?

options.A: The researcher hand-picks participants who have the most interesting medical history
options.B: Every individual in the population has a known, random chance of being selected
options.C: Participants are recruited strictly on a first-come, first-served hospital entry basis
options.D: Only the most cooperative patients on the hospital ward are chosen to participate

explanation: You nailed it! Probability sampling relies on pure chance, meaning everyone in the group has a fair and calculable shot at being picked.

question: What is the typical pattern of pain experienced in the early stages of osteoarthritis?

options.A: Sudden sharp pain that only happens during deep sleep
options.B: Severe constant pain that never changes day or night
options.C: Pain that worsens with activity and gets better with rest
options.D: Pain that disappears completely when walking long distances

explanation: Early osteoarthritis pain is typically triggered by joint use and eased when the client rests the affected limb. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: Which substance must be present in the stomach for vitamin B12 to be absorbed properly?

options.A: Hydrochloric acid
options.B: Bile salt binding
options.C: Intrinsic factor
options.D: Pepsinogen enzyme

explanation: Intrinsic factor is a special helper made by the stomach that binds to vitamin B12 so it can safely travel and be absorbed down the line.

question: Why must the sexual partner of someone treated for salpingitis also get antibiotic treatment?

options.A: To balance the hormonal levels of both partners concurrently
options.B: To prevent reinfection of the patient and stop further community spread
options.C: To ensure the male partner does not develop a bladder infection
options.D: To satisfy mandatory legal reporting requirements for minor illnesses

explanation: Treating both partners breaks the ping-pong cycle of passing the STI back and forth. Teamwork in healthcare matters!

question: Why do nurses prefer using a large-bore cannula (like an 18-gauge) for blood transfusions?

options.A: It prevents the physical damage and destruction of red blood cells
options.B: It prevents the IV site from swelling or leaking into the tissues
options.C: It allows the nurse to infuse multiple medications at the same time
options.D: It reduces the need to check vital signs during the first fifteen minutes

explanation: Think of it like a wide pipe versus a tiny straw—narrow needles can squeeze and break fragile red blood cells, causing damage.

question: Whose responsibility is it to ensure visitors follow isolation rules in a patient's room?

options.A: The nurse caring for the patient
options.B: The patient staying in the room
options.C: The hospital security guards
options.D: The dietary staff delivering meals

explanation: Nurses are responsible for educating visitors and making sure everyone entering the isolation room adheres to safety protocols. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h8)

question: Why is it a bad idea to use young family members as language interpreters?

options.A: Hospital policies fine families for using child translators
options.B: It can lead to translation errors and breach patient privacy
options.C: Children refuse to speak during home health visits
options.D: Children are always better at medical terminology than adults

explanation: Medical terms are tough to translate, and it puts an unfair emotional burden on a child to handle sensitive health matters for their relative.

question: How many blood vessels are normally found in a healthy newborn's umbilical cord?

options.A: Two arteries and one vein
options.B: Two veins and one artery
options.C: Two veins and two arteries
options.D: One vein and one artery

explanation: Think of it as 3 vessels total: 2 smaller arteries taking used blood away from the baby, and 1 bigger vein bringing fresh oxygenated blood back to them.

question: Why would a patient with severe facial swelling get a tracheostomy instead of a normal breathing tube through the mouth?

options.A: It lets the patient speak normally right away
options.B: It bypasses the blocked upper airway completely
options.C: It stops all future lung infections completely
options.D: It needs zero nursing checks afterward

explanation: When facial trauma blocks the upper airway, a tracheostomy makes a fresh, clear pathway below the blockage. You're doing great!

question: Why is it so helpful to give patients written discharge instructions alongside talking to them?

options.A: It helps patients remember and follow their care plan once they get home
options.B: It stops patients from ever asking nurses questions
options.C: It legally proves the patient understood every single word
options.D: It completely replaces follow-up clinic phone calls

explanation: Hospitals can be overwhelming! Patients forget half of what you tell them verbally the moment they walk out the door. Written guides keep them safe at home.

question: What does a public health nurse focus on most during community outreach?

options.A: Performing emergency appendectomies in a village square
options.B: Educating mothers on childhood immunization and sanitation
options.C: Installing borehole water pumps for the village
options.D: Prescribing chemotherapy for advanced cancer patients

explanation: Exactly! Public health nurses are community champions. They focus heavily on disease prevention, health education, and keeping moms and babies smiling and healthy.

question: What is the main reason for using strict aseptic technique during an intraarticular injection?

options.A: To keep the doctor's hands clean during the procedure
options.B: To make the injection completely painless for the patient
options.C: To prevent introducing bacteria that cause septic arthritis
options.D: To ensure the medication absorbs faster into the bloodstream

explanation: Strict sterility protects the joint capsule from dangerous bacterial infections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why is couples counseling sometimes included in managing FGM complications?

options.A: To arrange for the husband to perform minor home surgeries
options.B: To force the couple to divorce immediately
options.C: To legally fine the husband for cultural traditions
options.D: To educate partners and reduce sexual or marital conflict

explanation: Spot on! Involving partners helps clear up dangerous myths about anatomy and pain, easing tension and improving understanding at home. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h5)

question: How do maternity support belts help reduce pregnancy-related discomfort?

options.A: They stop all uterine contractions from happening entirely.
options.B: They increase the amount of amniotic fluid inside the womb.
options.C: They cure underlying urinary tract infections automatically.
options.D: They lift the heavy abdomen to take strain off ligaments and back muscles.

explanation: Support belts distribute the weight of the growing belly more evenly, relieving the pull on the lower back and pelvis. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h4)

question: A patient drinks a mug of tea, receives an IV antibiotic piggyback, and eats a plate of rice. What counts as fluid intake?

options.A: The tea and the IV antibiotic
options.B: Only the IV antibiotic
options.C: Only the mug of tea
options.D: The tea, IV antibiotic, and rice

explanation: Liquids consumed orally and fluids given intravenously are recorded as intake, while solid food is excluded. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h3)

question: What happens when you mix ordinary trash with infectious medical waste?

options.A: The entire batch becomes dangerous infectious waste
options.B: The total volume of waste decreases significantly
options.C: The waste can be safely recycled as normal trash
options.D: The infectious waste automatically becomes harmless

explanation: You've got this! Mixing clean trash with infectious material contaminates everything, which drives up disposal costs and safety risks. Always segregate early! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of a biological workplace hazard?

options.A: Loud machinery noise
options.B: Repetitive typing motion
options.C: Toxic cleaning solvents
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: Biological hazards come from living things like germs, bacteria, and viruses (such as Hepatitis B) that can affect healthcare workers and others. You're doing great!

question: What two things must be true for the rule of 'respondeat superior' to apply to a nurse's mistake?

options.A: An employer-employee relationship and action within the scope of employment
options.B: Written hospital policies and a signed malpractice insurance contract
options.C: A nursing license renewal and membership in a professional association
options.D: Direct supervision by a physician and a formal patient consent form

explanation: For the hospital to be pulled in, you must actually work there, and the mistake has to happen while you are doing your assigned job duties.

question: Why do displaced persons living in crowded temporary camps often face sudden disease outbreaks?

options.A: A genetic predisposition unique to populations forced from their homes
options.B: Complete lack of exposure to any natural pathogens prior to displacement
options.C: The intentional release of biological agents within temporary settlement zones
options.D: Overcrowding combined with compromised sanitation and clean water shortages

explanation: Spot on! Tight spaces, lack of clean water, and poor waste disposal create the perfect storm for infections to spread quickly.

question: When a patient with a throat infection develops a high fever, tiredness, and swollen neck glands, what do these show?

options.A: Lower airway collapse
options.B: Systemic response to the infection
options.C: Permanent vocal cord damage
options.D: Localized allergic rhinitis

explanation: Spot on! Fever and swollen lymph glands are signs that the whole body's immune system is active and fighting the germs.

question: Which degree of perineal tear affects only the vaginal skin and mucous membrane?

options.A: Third-degree tear
options.B: First-degree tear
options.C: Fourth-degree tear
options.D: Second-degree tear

explanation: A first-degree tear is very minor and superficial, touching only the skin and mucous membranes without getting into the deeper muscles.

question: Why are regular hearing tests important for workers in noisy industrial plants?

options.A: They detect early hearing loss before the damage becomes permanent
options.B: They make the factory machines run much more quietly
options.C: They prove that loud noise has no effect on human ears
options.D: They replace the need for wearing earplugs

explanation: Routine testing spots subtle hearing changes early, prompting better protection before deafness occurs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: A community health nurse is planning care in a village near a fast-flowing river. Which action best supports primary prevention?

options.A: Isolating infected patients in hospital wards for six months
options.B: Administering daily eye drops to every school-aged child
options.C: Educating residents on wearing protective clothing and using ivermectin
options.D: Surgically removing all subcutaneous nodules from every villager

explanation: Teaching folks how to avoid blackfly bites and combining that with community ivermectin distribution is the gold standard in public health nursing.

question: Two hours after a colonoscopy, a patient's abdomen feels hard like a board and they have severe pain. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward to pass trapped gas
options.B: Administer a strong oral laxative to clear the bowels quickly
options.C: Notify the physician immediately and keep the patient nil per os
options.D: Offer the patient a warm glass of water to soothe the stomach

explanation: A rigid, hard tummy with sharp pain is a classic red flag for a bowel perforation. Call the doctor straight away and stop all food and drinks (nil per os).

question: What is a great way to improve vaccine turnout in a hesitant rural community?

options.A: Stopping all outreach visits and waiting for parents to find the clinic
options.B: Collaborating with respected local leaders and traditional rulers for health talks
options.C: Threatening parents with police arrest if they miss clinic appointments
options.D: Hiding the vaccine vials so people do not know what is being injected

explanation: Spot on! Traditional and community leaders have great influence and can help clear up rumors so families feel safe bringing their children.

question: Why must you perform hand hygiene immediately after taking off your gloves?

options.A: Hospital policy requires washing hands twice per hour
options.B: Gloves make your hands smell unpleasant
options.C: Microorganisms may have transferred to your skin during removal
options.D: It helps the skin dry out after sweating inside rubber

explanation: Even with careful removal, tiny tears or contact with the outside of gloves can transfer germs to your hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h5)

question: Where do home health care services primarily take place?

options.A: A specialized outpatient clinic
options.B: A long-term nursing facility
options.C: An acute care hospital ward
options.D: The client's personal residence

explanation: Spot on! Home health care brings professional nursing straight to where the client lives. It's all about comfort and care right at home.

question: A male patient with a pelvic fracture has blood at the tip of his penis and cannot urinate. What is the safest nursing action?

options.A: Hold off on placing a standard urinary catheter and report the finding immediately.
options.B: Massage the lower abdomen firmly to force the patient to void naturally.
options.C: Insert a rigid plastic catheter gently until resistance disappears.
options.D: Force a standard Foley catheter past the blockage to relieve the bladder pressure.

explanation: Never force a catheter if you suspect a torn urethra—it can make the injury much worse! Always pause, leave it alone, and inform the doctor right away.

question: Why does a lack of basic education often lead to higher rates of unintended pregnancies?

options.A: It guarantees employment in high-stress urban environments
options.B: It increases the biological fertility rate of every woman
options.C: It physically alters the organs of the reproductive system
options.D: It limits access to accurate information on how to prevent conception

explanation: Exactly! Without proper education, people are left relying on myths instead of solid facts about family planning.

question: Which of these is NOT an infection prevention item found in a midwifery kit?

options.A: Alcohol-based hand rub for quick cleaning
options.B: A heavy-duty manual blood pressure cuff
options.C: Sterile and clean disposable gloves
options.D: A safety box for used needles

explanation: A blood pressure cuff is a vital tool for checking vitals, but it isn't an infection control supply like gloves or hand sanitizer.

question: What is a safer alternative you can suggest to a new mother for easing perineal swelling instead of hot water?

options.A: Boiling steam directed continuously onto the surgical repair
options.B: Clean cold compresses or ice packs wrapped in a soft cloth
options.C: Total avoidance of any hygiene or washing for six weeks
options.D: Direct application of pure chemical bleach to numb the area

explanation: Ice packs are a nurse's best friend for fresh swelling! Cold numbs the pain and shrinks local blood vessels safely without burning or softening the tissues.

question: What is the name of the special chart midwives use to track how labour is progressing?

options.A: Apgar sheet
options.B: Growth curve
options.C: Partograph
options.D: Antenatal chart

explanation: The partograph is our best friend in the labour ward! It gives a clear picture of how labour is moving along so we spot trouble early.

question: What delayed complication of a sting can show up days later with fever, joint pain, and a skin rash?

options.A: Hyperglycemia
options.B: Serum sickness
options.C: Cellulitis
options.D: Anaphylactic shock

explanation: Correct! Serum sickness is an immune system reaction that can pop up several days after exposure, causing fever, aching joints, and rashes.

question: What is the exact infectious stage of the parasite that actually enters the human body?

options.A: Miracidia
options.B: Metacercariae
options.C: Cercariae
options.D: Adult fluke

explanation: You nailed it! Humans catch the infection by swallowing encysted metacercariae hiding in raw or poorly cooked freshwater crabs and crayfish.

question: Why would a doctor order an Arterial Blood Gas (ABG) test for an asphyxiated patient?

options.A: To measure blood acidity and gas levels directly
options.B: To screen the blood stream for infectious bacteria
options.C: To count the exact number of red blood cells
options.D: To check if the patient took any prescription drugs

explanation: An ABG gives a direct look at how much oxygen and carbon dioxide are floating around, plus the blood's pH. Super helpful during respiratory distress!

question: A grieving family arrives shortly after their relative passes away. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Give them a detailed lecture on the stages of human grief
options.B: Instruct them to leave quickly so post-mortem care can begin
options.C: Ask them to sign discharge paperwork before entering the room
options.D: Provide a quiet space and allow them uninterrupted time with their loved one

explanation: You're doing great! Giving families private time helps them begin to process their loss peacefully.

question: Why is it best to use local languages and trusted community figures when teaching disaster safety?

options.A: It prevents the government from spending money on ads
options.B: It is a strict legal requirement for all hospital workers
options.C: It stops people from asking questions about safety plans
options.D: It builds trust and ensures the message is easily understood

explanation: Spot on! People are much more likely to listen and take action when advice comes from a familiar, respected voice speaking their native language.

question: What should you do if your final results turn out different from your original guess (hypothesis)?

options.A: Delete the unexpected data points from the final report
options.B: Report the actual findings honestly and objectively
options.C: Hide the entire study so nobody sees the mistake
options.D: Change the original hypothesis to match the new data

explanation: Integrity is key in nursing research. Always report what the data actually says, even if it surprises you!

question: Which of these is NOT part of basic respiratory hygiene in a clinic waiting area?

options.A: Placing hand sanitizer dispensers near the entrance
options.B: Mandating full isolation gowns for all visitors
options.C: Providing facial tissues for visitors
options.D: Offering surgical masks to coughing individuals

explanation: Correct! Visitors do not need isolation gowns just to sit in a waiting area. Respiratory hygiene is all about masks, tissues, clean hands, and catching coughs.

question: Why might private clinics push for more injections in a fee-for-service system?

options.A: Government subsidies pay hospitals more for oral pills.
options.B: Insurance companies strictly forbid giving prescriptions for tablets.
options.C: Injections and related supplies allow them to charge higher fees.
options.D: Needles and syringes are completely free for medical facilities.

explanation: Financial gain drives unnecessary injections when clinics profit from charging extra for procedural administration and supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h4)

question: What should you do immediately if a patient gets a chemical splashed into both eyes?

options.A: Flush the eyes continuously with clean water or normal saline for at least fifteen minutes
options.B: Rub the eyes firmly with a dry towel to remove solid particles
options.C: Put neutral cooking oil directly into the eyes to coat the chemical
options.D: Apply tight gauze patches over both eyes and wait for an ophthalmologist

explanation: Water is your best friend here! Long, continuous flushing washes away caustic chemicals before they can damage the cornea.

question: What is a major reason for high maternal mortality rates in many rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Limited access to skilled birth attendants and emergency obstetric care
options.B: Universal free access to advanced reproductive technology
options.C: Mandatory hospital deliveries for all pregnant women
options.D: An overabundance of licensed gynecologists in primary health centers

explanation: When clinics are far away and transport is hard to find, delays in getting emergency care during childbirth sadly put many mothers at high risk.

question: Why is supportive care so crucial when treating newly emerging infectious diseases?

options.A: Specific targeted medications may not yet exist for new pathogens
options.B: Patients recover much faster without receiving any fluids
options.C: Medications are forbidden in federal isolation treatment centers
options.D: Supportive care permanently changes the genetic code of a virus

explanation: Because new pathogens take time to study, treatments often rely on supporting the body's organs until the immune system fights it off. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h8)

question: A newborn delivered after a tough, instrument-assisted birth is very sleepy (lethargic) and has a high-pitched cry. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Physiological moulding
options.B: Normal post-birth fatigue
options.C: Mild caput succedaneum
options.D: Intracranial hemorrhage

explanation: You nailed it. Unusual sleepiness and a high-pitched cry are classic red flags that there might be pressure or bleeding inside the baby's head.

question: A senior doctor frequently interrupts junior nurses and dominates a committee meeting. What is the best action for the chairperson to take?

options.A: Ask the junior nurses to leave the room until the discussion ends
options.B: Politely acknowledge the input and redirect the floor to quieter participants
options.C: Ignore the behavior so the senior doctor does not get offended
options.D: Cancel all future committee meetings to avoid conflict

explanation: A great chair handles dominant speakers respectfully while making space for everyone else to share.

question: Why do early adolescents often look a bit uncoordinated or clumsy?

options.A: Neurological damage occurs temporarily during puberty
options.B: Hands and feet grow faster than the rest of the body
options.C: Shrinking of the inner ear balancing structures
options.D: Lack of proper physical exercise in school

explanation: Think of it like a growth spurt where the hands and feet shoot up first! This temporary mismatch throws off coordination for a bit, but it completely evens out.

question: Which organ in the body is the main target for both Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C?

options.A: The lungs
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The kidneys
options.D: The liver

explanation: Spot on! Both hepatitis B and C viruses attack liver cells, causing inflammation and long-term damage if left untreated.

question: A nurse is working in a crowded emergency shelter after a flood. What is the most important step to prevent a disease outbreak?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on major surgical procedures on-site
options.B: Ensuring access to safe drinking water and maintaining sanitation
options.C: Conducting formal structural engineering tests on the shelter
options.D: Refusing admission to anyone showing signs of mild stress

explanation: In crowded shelters, poor hygiene and unsafe water can easily cause disease outbreaks. Clean water and sanitation are your best defenses here! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h8)

question: What is the very first step when you want to start a nursing research project?

options.A: Applying for hospital funding
options.B: Collecting patient blood samples
options.C: Identifying the research problem
options.D: Writing the final conclusion

explanation: Every good study starts by figuring out what the exact problem is. You have to spot the gap in patient care before you can start gathering any data!

question: Why must you NEVER put anything in a patient's mouth while they are having a generalized seizure?

options.A: It can fracture teeth, damage gums, and block the patient's airway
options.B: It triggers immediate vomiting and severe stomach aspiration
options.C: It causes the seizure to spread instantly to the opposite brain hemisphere
options.D: It stops the brain from absorbing the rescue medication properly

explanation: Trying to force objects into a seizing patient's mouth can easily break their teeth, cut their gums, or push items down into their throat, blocking their airway. Let the seizure run its course safely!

question: What is the main difference between congenital and acquired disabilities?

options.A: Acquired conditions never cause any emotional distress or grief
options.B: Congenital conditions are present from birth, while acquired ones happen later in life
options.C: Acquired conditions are always genetic and passed down in families
options.D: Congenital conditions only affect older adults in the community

explanation: You've got it! 'Congenital' means it's been there since birth, while 'acquired' means something happened later in life to change their physical abilities.

question: What is a counter-referral in community health practice?

options.A: Transferring a patient from a private clinic to a traditional healer
options.B: Reporting a nurse to the nursing council for writing a bad referral note
options.C: Sending a discharged patient back to their local clinic for follow-up care
options.D: Refusing to accept a patient into the teaching hospital due to lack of beds

explanation: A counter-referral brings the patient back to the primary level for continuous local monitoring after hospital treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h8)

question: Why should nurses involve traditional and religious leaders when starting a new community health project?

options.A: They provide free medical supplies to the clinic
options.B: Their approval builds trust and community acceptance
options.C: They are trained to audit hospital financial records
options.D: They write all official government health policies

explanation: Community leaders hold great influence. When they support a health initiative, the people are much more willing to listen and participate. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h5)

question: What happens when a tumor suppressor gene experiences a loss-of-function mutation?

options.A: The cell immediately transforms into a benign fibrous cyst
options.B: The cell loses its molecular brakes and divides uncontrollably
options.C: The cell creates an outer capsule to prevent metastasis
options.D: Normal cellular division stops permanently in the G0 phase

explanation: Tumor suppressor genes normally slow down cell growth; losing them removes these protective brakes, allowing rapid tumor growth. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h6)

question: During early development, which main germ layer gives rise to all of our muscle tissues?

options.A: Blastoderm
options.B: Mesoderm
options.C: Ectoderm
options.D: Endoderm

explanation: You've got this! The middle germ layer, the mesoderm, is responsible for building our skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscles. Think 'M for middle and muscle!'

question: Which hormone is famous for softening pelvic ligaments during pregnancy?

options.A: Cortisol
options.B: Relaxin
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Spot on! Relaxin lives up to its name by relaxing and loosening the ligaments to help the pelvis prepare for childbirth.

question: You are feeding a patient who looks very tired and worn out. What is the safest way to handle their meal?

options.A: Allowing frequent rest periods and offering smaller, more frequent meals
options.B: Laying the patient flat in bed to conserve their physical energy
options.C: Mixing all the food together so it is easier to swallow quickly
options.D: Feeding the remaining food much faster to finish on time

explanation: Tired muscles make swallowing mistakes easy. Pacing the meal and serving smaller portions keeps your patient safe and energized.

question: Why is a single initial assessment insufficient for palliative care patients?

options.A: Palliative conditions and symptoms change rapidly over time
options.B: Patients usually forget their medical history on day one
options.C: Doctors prefer to change diagnoses daily without reason
options.D: Hospitals require a new paperwork form every single hour

explanation: Because disease trajectories fluctuate, ongoing re-assessment is necessary to catch new or worsening symptoms. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of rehabilitation nursing?

options.A: To help patients regain their highest level of independence
options.B: To cure acute infectious diseases quickly
options.C: To provide permanent institutional care for the elderly
options.D: To manage chronic pain through heavy medication

explanation: Rehabilitation nursing focuses heavily on restoring a patient's functional abilities so they can care for themselves as much as possible. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h1)

question: Why is cultural humility crucial for a community health nurse?

options.A: It helps the nurse respect local beliefs and build trust with community members
options.B: It prevents the nurse from ever needing to wash their hands
options.C: It ensures the nurse receives a higher salary from the government
options.D: It allows the nurse to diagnose complex surgical conditions instantly

explanation: Understanding and respecting local traditions breaks down barriers and encourages people to accept health advice and services. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h8)

question: As a nurse, why is it helpful to understand national food policies?

options.A: Clinical nutritional counseling fails if patients cannot access or afford recommended foods
options.B: Nurses decide the specific types of seeds farmers must plant
options.C: Nurses are legally required to inspect commercial farms for safety
options.D: Clinical staff must directly distribute farming money to local villages

explanation: When you give dietary advice to a patient, you have to know what food is actually available and affordable in their community!

question: What is the medical term for coughing up blood from the lungs?

options.A: Epistaxis
options.B: Hemothorax
options.C: Hematemesis
options.D: Hemoptysis

explanation: Hemoptysis refers specifically to blood that comes up from the respiratory system through coughing. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is the best position for your patient during a thoracentesis?

options.A: Lying flat on the back with arms raised above the head
options.B: Sitting upright and leaning forward over a bedside table
options.C: Positioned flat on the unaffected side with knees bent
options.D: Prone with a pillow placed directly under the abdomen

explanation: Awesome! This forward-leaning posture opens up the spaces between the ribs nicely, making it much safer and easier for the doctor to reach the fluid.

question: How do you deflate the retention balloon before taking out a Foley catheter?

options.A: Puncture the outer catheter wall with a large needle
options.B: Cut the balloon valve tubing with surgical scissors
options.C: Inject more water to pop the balloon safely inside the bladder
options.D: Attach a syringe to the inflation port and draw out all the water

explanation: Spot on! Hooking up a syringe and pulling out the exact amount of water that was put in ensures the balloon collapses completely before you slide the tube out.

question: Which tool is best for sliding an immobile patient smoothly across the bed sheet?

options.A: A motorized wheelchair
options.B: Slide sheets
options.C: A mechanical lift
options.D: A gait belt

explanation: Spot on! Slide sheets cut down friction against the mattress, making it so much easier and safer to reposition patients without hurting their skin or your back.

question: Office workers are complaining of severe back and wrist pain from poorly set up desks. What is the best intervention?

options.A: Immediate quarantine of the office building for suspected chemical leaks
options.B: Prescription of heavy industrial respirators to prevent indoor dust inhalation
options.C: Mandatory industrial safety harness training for all desk workers
options.D: Ergonomic workspace assessment and workstation adjustments

explanation: An ergonomic check helps fix poor posture, chair height, and computer placement, stopping strain before it gets worse!

question: What is the most common cause of salpingitis?

options.A: Sexually transmitted bacteria
options.B: Autoimmune joint disorders
options.C: Fungal overgrowth from antibiotics
options.D: Congenital structural defects

explanation: Infections like Chlamydia and Gonorrhea are the main culprits behind most fallopian tube infections.

question: What does the vertical Y-axis on a run chart typically represent?

options.A: The specific names of the staff nurses
options.B: The time sequence in days or weeks
options.C: The total number of hospital beds
options.D: The measurement or metric of interest

explanation: The Y-axis shows the actual clinical data values being measured, such as rates or counts. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is metoclopramide especially helpful for diabetic patients suffering from slow stomach emptying (gastroparesis) and nausea?

options.A: It coats the gastric mucosa to heal ulcers
options.B: It paralyzes the vagus nerve to stop spasms
options.C: It lowers blood glucose levels rapidly
options.D: It increases gastrointestinal motility and emptying

explanation: Brilliant! Metoclopramide acts as a prokinetic, meaning it physically speeds up the stomach so food moves forward instead of coming back up. Excellent clinical connection!

question: What type of thinking skills usually show up during middle adolescence?

options.A: Fully mature adult executive reasoning
options.B: Formal operational or abstract thinking
options.C: Pre-operational magical thinking
options.D: Only concrete operational thinking

explanation: Well done! Middle adolescents start thinking beyond what's right in front of them—they can grasp abstract ideas and imagine 'what if' scenarios.

question: Which symptom strongly points to an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction?

options.A: Lower back or flank pain
options.B: Gradual weight loss over days
options.C: Excessive daytime sleepiness
options.D: Severe localized skin dryness

explanation: When red cells break down inside the body, the kidneys take a hit, which often shows up as sharp lower back or flank pain.

question: Keeping a hospital patient's call bell within easy reach is an action primarily aimed at meeting which type of need?

options.A: Love and belonging
options.B: Physiological rest
options.C: Self-actualization
options.D: Safety and security

explanation: A call bell gives the patient a way to call for help, satisfying their need for physical and environmental safety. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is needed to make sure digital gadgets and tech actually help student learning?

options.A: Good teacher training and reliable school infrastructure
options.B: Making students wear VR headsets for every single class
options.C: Throwing away all printed nursing textbooks
options.D: Restricting computer use only to top school admin staff

explanation: Tech is only helpful if your school has steady power, working equipment, and teachers who know how to use it with you.

question: A village floods every rainy season. What is the best proactive nursing action to prepare?

options.A: Focusing solely on treating broken bones after the flood recedes
options.B: Telling families to abandon their ancestral land permanently
options.C: Waiting until the floodwaters rise before requesting relief materials
options.D: Educating residents on evacuation routes and establishing early warning systems

explanation: Preparation means teaching escape routes and setting up warnings *before* the water starts rising. Great job working through these!

question: Why shouldn't we rely solely on 'we've always done it this way' when caring for patients?

options.A: Old routines are rarely supported by current evidence
options.B: Textbooks change their definitions every single month
options.C: Hospital management strictly forbids the use of tradition
options.D: Patients refuse care that has been used for many years

explanation: It is easy to stick to old habits, but checking modern research helps us give our patients the safest, most up-to-date care possible.

question: What is the primary underlying assumption of standard precautions?

options.A: Gloves replace the need for washing your hands
options.B: Only visible blood contains dangerous bacterial pathogens
options.C: All body fluids can potentially transmit infectious agents
options.D: Healthy patients require no protective measures at all

explanation: Treating all body fluids as potentially infectious prevents accidental exposure to hidden pathogens. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which sign might tell you that a patient is struggling during a ventilator weaning trial?

options.A: Sweating and an increasing heart rate
options.B: Asking for a glass of cold water
options.C: Calm facial expression and steady sleep
options.D: Lower blood pressure and normal breathing

explanation: If a patient breaks out in a sweat (diaphoresis) and their heart rate spikes, it's a clear distress signal telling us the breathing workload is still too heavy for them.

question: What is the most common symptom for a patient who is missing just one fallopian tube from birth?

options.A: No symptoms at all
options.B: Permanent primary amenorrhea
options.C: Heavy abnormal uterine bleeding
options.D: Severe chronic pelvic pain

explanation: Exactly! Many women with one missing tube live completely normal lives and only find out by accident during medical scans.

question: Which property of the skin allows patches and creams to deliver medication into the body?

options.A: High concentration of sweat and oil glands
options.B: Continuous shedding of the outer epidermis
options.C: Semi-permeability to lipid-soluble substances
options.D: Thick layer of insulating subcutaneous fat

explanation: Certain medications can pass through the skin barrier because the skin is semi-permeable to fat-soluble compounds. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the big giveaway that a study is observational?

options.A: Patients are given a new medication to test its safety
options.B: The researcher does not apply any experimental intervention
options.C: Data is collected exclusively through laboratory blood tests
options.D: All participants must be followed up for at least ten years

explanation: Exactly! In observational studies, researchers just sit back, watch, and record what happens naturally without interfering. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h3)

question: What is a major personal benefit of joining a professional nursing body as a student or young nurse?

options.A: Automatic pay raises negotiated by the national body
options.B: Guaranteed promotion to head nurse within a year
options.C: Opportunities for networking and career growth
options.D: Exemption from paying annual state license renewal fees

explanation: Joining lets you connect with senior nurses and mentors who can help guide your career path and open doors to exciting opportunities!

question: What is the most severe and dangerous complication linked specifically to Taenia solium?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Neurocysticercosis
options.C: Chronic kidney failure
options.D: Obstructive jaundice

explanation: Correct! When larval cysts find their way into the central nervous system, it causes neurocysticercosis, which frequently leads to seizures and neurological issues.

question: What should a nurse do if a low-risk pregnant woman develops severe anemia during her third trimester?

options.A: Advise her to drink more local herbal tea
options.B: Allow her to deliver at home with extra pillows
options.C: Disqualify her from home delivery and refer her to a hospital
options.D: Ignore the blood test results if she feels fine

explanation: Severe anemia puts the mother at high risk of postpartum hemorrhage, meaning she must deliver where blood transfusion is available. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h5)

question: When is a scheduled caesarean section typically recommended for a pregnant woman living with HIV?

options.A: When the baby is presenting in a normal vertex position
options.B: When her viral load is high or unknown near delivery
options.C: When the mother prefers surgical delivery for convenience
options.D: When she has been taking her ART medications strictly

explanation: A planned caesarean delivery before labor starts helps lower the risk of infant exposure when viral suppression is not confirmed. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is one common drawback of giving medications through mucous membranes?

options.A: Guaranteed 100% absorption for every patient
options.B: Longer time to onset than oral tablets
options.C: Risk of local irritation and variable absorption
options.D: Elimination of the need for nurse verification

explanation: Tissues in the mouth, rectum, or eyes can sometimes get sore or irritated by potent drugs, and how fast they absorb can change depending on how moist or healthy the tissue is.

question: What is a common reason why community members show apathy toward new health programs?

options.A: Excessive amounts of free medicine being supplied
options.B: Past broken promises from government agencies
options.C: Too many nurses wanting to visit the village daily
options.D: Mandatory attendance at international conferences

explanation: Unfulfilled past commitments create cynicism, making residents skeptical of new health initiatives until concrete results are shown. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h6)

question: What do we call the action where food is pushed back inside the stomach to get mashed up even more?

options.A: Peristalsis
options.B: Retropulsion
options.C: Regurgitation
options.D: Segmentation

explanation: Think of retropulsion as the stomach's bounce-back action. Food gets pushed toward the closed exit valve and bounces back for another round of mixing!

question: What is the ultimate goal when you empower a patient through nutrition counselling?

options.A: Making the patient work as a nutrition assistant
options.B: Removing all healthcare professionals from the system
options.C: Forcing patients to cook every meal from scratch
options.D: Patient independence in making healthy food choices

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Our job is to give patients the confidence and tools to take care of themselves, even when we aren't standing right there.

question: If a nursing mother's diet lacks enough nutrients, how does her body manage to produce breast milk?

options.A: The body absorbs extra nutrients directly from the air
options.B: Milk production stops completely until diet improves
options.C: The body draws from maternal stores to maintain milk
options.D: Breast milk loses all its essential nutrients instantly

explanation: Nature makes sure the baby gets what it needs! If diet falls short, the mother's body will use its own stored nutrients to keep the milk flowing. Great job understanding maternal priority!

question: What is the most important assessment for a nurse to make right after giving a rescue bronchodilator?

options.A: Capillary refill time in the fingers
options.B: Lung sounds and breathing effort
options.C: Deep tendon reflexes in the knees
options.D: Bowel sounds in all four quadrants

explanation: Since bronchodilators open up tight airways, listening to the patient's chest and watching their breathing effort is the quickest way to see if the treatment worked.

question: How do clinical audits and incident reports help nursing management?

options.A: By ensuring that nurses never experience stress during their shifts
options.B: By replacing the need for formal hospital administrative authority
options.C: By automatically transferring legal liability to the hospital board
options.D: By providing control mechanisms to monitor performance and correct standard deviations

explanation: Audits and incident reports act as safety nets. They help managers spot mistakes early, track quality, and keep patient care standards high.

question: Why do nurses give medications through an IV line instead of having the patient swallow a pill?

options.A: It lasts much longer in the bloodstream than oral pills.
options.B: It prevents all known systemic side effects from occurring.
options.C: It is completely painless for every patient receiving treatment.
options.D: It provides a much faster onset of drug action in the body.

explanation: Spot on! Because IV fluids go straight into the bloodstream, the body skips the digestive tract entirely and goes to work right away. You've got this!

question: How does the heart first try to make up for a severe lack of red blood cells (anemia)?

options.A: By decreasing the volume of plasma to thicken the blood
options.B: By increasing heart rate and cardiac output to circulate blood faster
options.C: By constricting peripheral blood vessels to raise blood pressure
options.D: By slowing down heart rate to let blood absorb more oxygen

explanation: Since each drop of blood is carrying less oxygen, the heart pumps faster and harder to keep enough oxygen moving around the body. It's working overtime!

question: How do regular performance appraisals help integrate personal and organisational goals?

options.A: By replacing the need for clinical nursing documentation
options.B: By ensuring that no nurse ever receives a promotion
options.C: By providing a platform for supervisors and nurses to discuss mutual expectations
options.D: By giving management an excuse to cut nurse salaries every month

explanation: Appraisals shouldn't feel like a witch hunt. They are a great chance to sit down, talk about your career growth, and line it up with the hospital's goals.

question: Why must certain antiretroviral drugs be taken alongside food?

options.A: To stop the patient from feeling hungry at night
options.B: To replace drinking clean water
options.C: To reduce stomach irritation and improve drug absorption
options.D: To destroy the outer tablet coating instantly

explanation: You nailed it! Some meds are much easier on the stomach and work better when taken with a meal or snack.

question: Where would you expect to find endoparasites inside the human body?

options.A: Attached strictly to the outer skin
options.B: On the surface of the hair shafts
options.C: Inside tissues, organs, or blood
options.D: Exclusively inside clothing fibers

explanation: Great job! 'Endo-' means inside. Endoparasites live safely inside the body (like in your blood or organs), while ectoparasites (like lice) stay on the outside.

question: Which transmission route involves pathogens spreading via contaminated inanimate objects like door handles or instruments?

options.A: Airborne droplet transmission
options.B: Vector-borne transmission
options.C: Direct contact transmission
options.D: Indirect contact transmission

explanation: Indirect contact occurs when a susceptible host touches a surface or object that harbors infectious agents. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h3)

question: How does severe postpartum anaemia commonly impact a new mother in the weeks following discharge?

options.A: It causes permanent high blood pressure requiring daily meds
options.B: It boosts her physical energy due to fast red blood cell recycling
options.C: It speeds up the return of her monthly periods within a week
options.D: It causes deep, persistent fatigue that makes newborn care and bonding tough

explanation: Low haemoglobin means less oxygen travels to her tissues, leaving her utterly exhausted. Supporting her nutrition and recovery is a huge part of postpartum nursing care!

question: Which of these is NOT an expected result of taking a sympathomimetic drug?

options.A: Pupil dilation
options.B: Bronchodilation
options.C: Increased heart rate
options.D: Decreased heart rate

explanation: Sympathomimetic drugs mimic the sympathetic system—they speed things up, open airways, and widen pupils. They won't slow down the heart rate!

question: An infant is brought to the clinic at 14 weeks old with no previous shots. What should you do?

options.A: Tell the mother to return when the child reaches one year of age
options.B: Wait until the child is two years old before starting any injections
options.C: Administer catch-up doses according to the national guidelines
options.D: Give only the birth vaccines since the infant missed the early schedule

explanation: Don't worry if a baby comes in late! Just use national catch-up guidelines to get them protected as safely and quickly as possible.

question: Why should ear drops (otic drops) always be warmed to room temperature before putting them in?

options.A: Warming increases the antibiotic power
options.B: Cold drops can instantly burst the eardrum
options.C: Cold medication is too thick to pass through the ear canal
options.D: Cold drops can shock the inner ear and cause severe dizziness

explanation: Putting ice-cold drops straight into the ear canal tickles the balance center in the inner ear the wrong way, triggering sudden vertigo and nausea. Always warm them in your hands first!

question: Why do bad rural feeder roads hurt national food security?

options.A: They force the government to import all staple foods
options.B: They delay transport, causing high spoilage rates and high food prices in cities
options.C: They stop farmers from getting chemical fertilizers and seeds
options.D: They make it illegal for farmers to sell crops across state lines

explanation: When roads are poor, food gets stuck or damaged on the way, leading to waste and higher prices for people in the city.

question: What does the popular research acronym IMRAD stand for?

options.A: Inquiry, Materials, Recording, And Documentation
options.B: Introduction, Methods, Results, And Discussion
options.C: Investigation, Measurement, Review, And Data
options.D: Interpretation, Management, Research, And Draft

explanation: Think IMRAD: Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. It is the golden standard structure for organizing research papers!

question: In the SBAR communication tool, what does the letter 'R' stand for?

options.A: Recovery
options.B: Reassessment
options.C: Respiration
options.D: Recommendation

explanation: R is for Recommendation—this is where you clearly state what you think needs to happen next for the patient.

question: A nurse is getting ready to examine an anxious patient's external reproductive organs. What is the best first step?

options.A: Explain each step of the procedure before beginning
options.B: Begin the physical inspection immediately to save time
options.C: Skip the inspection if the patient expresses mild shyness
options.D: Ask family members to leave the room without explanation

explanation: Wonderful nursing instinct! Clear communication and gentle reassurance help ease patient anxiety during intimate checks.

question: A patient arrives with a blood glucose of 900 mg/dL, severe dehydration, confusion, but zero ketones in the urine. What's the likely condition?

options.A: Thyrotoxic Storm
options.B: Diabetic Ketoacidosis
options.C: Acute Adrenal Insufficiency
options.D: Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State

explanation: Spot on! Massive blood sugar and severe dehydration without ketones is the classic picture of HHS rather than DKA.

question: What happens in passive surveillance?

options.A: Patients must call a special hotline to report their own illness.
options.B: Health workers actively visit every household in the village.
options.C: Data is only collected during a national census every ten years.
options.D: Clinics send routine reports without being pushed by health officers.

explanation: Think of passive surveillance as your local clinic doing what they normally do—sending in their regular reports as part of daily duty without waiting for someone to chase them.

question: Why do researchers often prefer the median over the mean when looking at how long patients stay in the hospital?

options.A: The median is much harder to calculate using modern computer software
options.B: Length of stay can only be measured in whole numbers of days
options.C: A few patients staying an unusually long time can distort the average
options.D: Hospital administrators refuse to look at mathematical averages

explanation: Extreme outliers, like a patient staying 100 days, pull the mean way up, whereas the median stays stable and shows the typical experience.

question: Why is managing chronic symptoms right at home so helpful for a client?

options.A: It allows them to stay comfortable and remain in their familiar surroundings
options.B: It stops the natural aging process from occurring
options.C: It removes the need for any emotional or family support
options.D: It guarantees that they will never need to see a doctor again

explanation: Spot on! There's no place like home. Managing symptoms there keeps clients secure and surrounded by the people and things they love.

question: Why do patients in areas with few clinics feel extra pressured to stay quiet?

options.A: They receive free private insurance coverage
options.B: They prefer substandard medical equipment
options.C: They have few alternative clinics to go to if they are mistreated
options.D: They are legally forbidden from speaking to nurses

explanation: You got it! When there's nowhere else to go for care, patients feel too dependent to risk upsetting the staff.

question: What is the best way to report a patient's death when calling the doctor?

options.A: Provide a concise report of assessment findings and absent vital signs
options.B: Wait until the morning shift change before making the phone call
options.C: Ask the physician for permission to start post-mortem care immediately
options.D: Ask the doctor to sign the death certificate over the telephone

explanation: Well done! Giving quick, clear facts helps the doctor understand what's happening before they even step into the room.

question: In community health nursing, what does the term AEFI stand for?

options.A: Acute Emergency First Intervention
options.B: Active Epidemic Field Investigation
options.C: Adverse Events Following Immunization
options.D: Annual Evaluation For Infection

explanation: AEFI is simply any health issue that happens after a vaccine, whether the vaccine caused it or not. Good term to keep in mind!

question: You cover an open surgical wound with a sterile dressing. Which part of the infection chain are you primarily blocking?

options.A: Infectious agent
options.B: Infectious reservoir
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Portal of exit

explanation: Well done! A sterile dressing acts like a shield, stopping new germs from getting into the vulnerable, open tissue.

question: Which check uses the mid-upper arm size to spot severe weight loss or wasting in children?

options.A: Clinical examination
options.B: Biochemical analysis
options.C: Body measurement (anthropometry)
options.D: Radiological imaging

explanation: Spot on! Anthropometry simply means taking body measurements like height, weight, and arm size to see how well a child is growing.

question: Between which two meningeal layers is the subarachnoid space located?

options.A: Bone and dura mater
options.B: Arachnoid mater and pia mater
options.C: Dura mater and arachnoid mater
options.D: Skin and subcutaneous tissue

explanation: The subarachnoid space sits specifically between the middle arachnoid layer and the innermost pia mater layer. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h2)

question: What should you do if you are holding a sterile instrument package and suddenly feel unsure if it's truly sterile?

options.A: Use it only if the outer wrapper looks clean
options.B: Consider it contaminated and discard it
options.C: Wipe the instrument down with an antiseptic
options.D: Ask the surgeon to inspect the item before use

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! Patient safety always comes first, so never take chances with a questionable sterile item.

question: How does high blood pressure cause damage to a patient's kidneys?

options.A: High pressure strains and hardens the delicate blood vessels in the glomeruli
options.B: Hypertension directly causes the bladder to shrink
options.C: High blood pressure washes away all the red blood cells in the body
options.D: High pressure stops the heart from pumping blood to the lungs

explanation: Think of high pressure like a rushing river beating against a weak fence. It puts harsh mechanical stress on tiny kidney capillaries, causing them to scar over time.

question: What is the golden rule of pharmacology when giving new medications to older adults?

options.A: Administer all drugs strictly on an empty stomach
options.B: Give only through intramuscular injections
options.C: Double the adult dose immediately
options.D: Start low and go slow

explanation: Exactly! Always 'start low and go slow' with elderly patients to prevent nasty drug side effects since their bodies clear medications more slowly.

question: What are two major health risks associated with early unprotected sexual intercourse in adolescents?

options.A: Sexually transmitted infections and unintended pregnancies
options.B: Chronic respiratory illness and severe joint pain
options.C: Nutritional deficiencies and bone density loss
options.D: Visual impairment and cardiovascular disease

explanation: Unprotected sexual contact exposes young people directly to pathogens causing infections and fails to prevent fertilization, leading to high rates of teenage pregnancy. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h1)

question: Which animal is the main reservoir responsible for spreading the Lassa virus to humans?

options.A: Stray cats
options.B: Domestic dogs
options.C: Pigs and swine
options.D: Multimammate rats

explanation: You got it! Lassa fever is mainly passed to humans through contact with the urine and droppings of infected multimammate rats.

question: Why is family caregiver education especially important when nursing pediatric special needs patients at home?

options.A: Children do not require any medical monitoring once discharged
options.B: Nurses never visit more than once a year
options.C: Parents must learn how to handle equipment and recognize breathing distress
options.D: Parents are legally required to pass a formal medical board exam

explanation: Because nurses are not there twenty-four hours a day, parents must know how to manage daily equipment and emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h6)
